messages:
maya: Heads-up — planning to pin shared-config v2.4.1 during tomorrow's 00:00-02:00 UTC window to avoid runtime eviction during console/router canary.
aj: Pin? which cluster/variant are we pinning to exactly?
sam: API + runtime + router in us-east-1, console only for canary traffic slice (10%).
devon: Why do we need the pin? I thought eviction only happened when kernel batching changed.
maya: It's a precaution. Last time the router handshake caused tiny config churn and some runtime nodes dropped caches, causing slow warms. Pin keeps everyone on the exact config so deploybot can do a clean handoff.
katie: OK. Rollback criteria?
maya: If 1) p50 latency for API or router spikes >50% over baseline for 5m OR 2) error rate for runtime >0.5% for 3m, then rollback. Also manual rollback if console shows bad UX regressions.
aj: Can deploybot handle partial unpin/rollback per-region? We might want to unpin only us-east first.
sam: Deploybot supports region-scoped pins via `pin_scope: region:us-east-1`. We'll add that to the release note.
maya: Draft config snippet for deploybot (will push to PR):
```
- action: pin_config
  name: shared-config
  version: v2.4.1
  pin_scope:
    regions: [us-east-1]
  window: 2026-03-22T00:00Z/2026-03-22T02:00Z
  notify: [#eng-releases, @oncall-runtime]
```
devon: lgtm. Make sure it includes `eviction_protection: true` so the runtime doesn't drop warm KV on short drain.
katie: Who's owning the rollback? @devon on runtime, @sam on router, @aj for API.
aj: I'm around during the window.
devon: same.
maya: I'll post release note to the console channel and add runbook link. Runbook: https://wiki.redwood/internal/runbooks/runtime-eviction
sam: Also include the metric IDs for runbook checks: `api.latency.p50`, `router.latency.p50`, `runtime.errors.count`.
maya: Will add those and a short checklist for on-call: 1) watch p50, 2) check prefix-cache miss rate, 3) check kv-warm hits. If all green after 30m, we unpin at the end of window.
katie: If we see small regressions but no errors, prefer keep-pin and monitor, unless customer-facing errors occur.
aj: Do we need to update release notes for customers? Might be internal-only, but I'll add a short line: "Operational config pin to stabilize runtime warmup during canary rollout."
maya: Good. Final ask: @deploybot, please schedule the pin with a 10m pre-notify to #eng-releases and tag @oncall-runtime.
